info.title: Datagoat API
info.description:
Ask yes/no, score, choice and rank questions about cases. Datagoat answers from what happened to cases like them: deterministic, with reasons, signed, and it refuses rather than guess. MCP: https://api.datagoat.io/mcp

## Which journey

Five journeys organise the operations: each operation is tagged with the journeys that use it, https://api.datagoat.io/journeys.arazzo.yaml has each journey as an Arazzo 1.1.0 workflow, and `describe` lists them with ready-to-run calls.

| Journey | Fits when the user… | Not when… | First call |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Try it](https://datagoat.io/docs/quickstart) | has no data yet, or wants to see an answer and a refusal before using their own | they already have a table of past cases (Ask your data) | `dg_describe`, then `dg_ask` (a sample's ready-to-run ask) |
| [Ask your data](https://datagoat.io/docs/ask-your-data) | has a table of past cases with a yes/no outcome (churned, converted, faulted) and a question about it | they will score cases every day for their own customers (Ship a product) | `dg_add_dataset` (upload: true for a file a person holds), then `dg_suggest` |
| [Ship a product](https://datagoat.io/docs/build) | will score many customers' cases repeatedly, on a schedule, inside their own product | it is a one-off question about one table (Ask your data) | `dg_ask` (with namespace and model_ttl_days), then `dg_ask` (by model_ref, no fit) |
| [Run it](https://datagoat.io/docs/run) | already has a model_ref in use and is learning what happened to the cases it scored | no model has been fitted yet (Ask your data) | `dg_report_outcomes`, then `dg_drift` |
| [Prove it](https://datagoat.io/docs/prove) | must show someone the calls were right, or measure whether acting on them worked | they only need the answer (Ask your data) | `dg_verify`, then `dg_track_record` (or dg_evidence, whether acting on the calls worked) |

post.description: For a question about cases from a record of past outcomes (a table, a log, a series), or scoring new cases from an existing model_ref; the questions worth trying on an unfamiliar table come from dg_suggest instead. Answers typed questions about cases from a record of past outcomes. A call sends the record (data), questions keyed by id, and the cases to answer; answers return keyed by the same ids. Question types: yesno (the chance the outcome happens), score (that chance as a level: unlikely, possible, likely, very_likely), choice (the best option for each case, with each option's chance, most_likely and least_likely; choice is the only type that needs outcome_is_desirable), rank (cases in order of the chance). Questions about one record can share one call, and questions on the same outcome and outcome_is_desirable share one fit. The record can be a table (one row per case) or, with shape, an event log, a time series, a panel, sensor signals, agent traces, or snapshots (an event log read as of each moment in a snapshot table, e.g. a deal at each stage). Building a product: namespace keeps each of your customers' models and usage apart; model_ttl_days (1 to 365) sets how long a fitted model answers; a question that names model_ref instead of outcome_column scores new cases from that model with no fit (send cases.rows, or a newer record and cases.ids), and every answer lists model_columns, the columns its model reads. Each answer has a state: answered; refused (the record holds no pattern that holds on held-out rows, and the same call returns the same refusal); or not_yet (too few labeled rows or positives; needs gives how many more of each, and reasons name what is short). A case the model cannot read (a column it reads is absent, or a value it never saw) comes back as state not_scoreable, naming them, with no chance; it bills nothing. An answered question carries, per case, p and up to four reasons (feature_label, value, likelihood_direction, strength, and range: the band of values the case's value fell in, e.g. "tenure_months 9 to under 17"), and a signed Verdict covering its cases. yesno, score and rank answers also carry pattern: the conditions, with cut points, under which the outcome is most common (e.g. "support_tickets over 3"), and per case pattern_match {matched, of, met}. Reasons and patterns are associations, not causes; likelihood_direction is the direction the chance moved, not whether that is good news. Answers are deterministic: the same record and question give the same answer. A first fit on a large record returns status pending with a task_id for dg_poll. Over MCP, an answer larger than one tool result (about 60,000 characters, roughly 60 cases with their Verdict) returns its first page: each list carries page {offset, returned, total}, page.next_cursor leads to the rest through dg_page, and page.answer_url downloads the whole answer as JSON. export: csv adds a CSV download of every case. response_format concise leaves the Verdicts out of the response (verdicts_withheld says how many); they stay in the full answer at page.answer_url, and states, chances and reasons are the same. Free to try on the samples, e.g. data.dataset_id sample:saas_churn, entity_column customer_id, outcome_column churned, cases {ids: ["cust_0001"]}. Cost: one decision per answered case, and a fit the first time a record is asked about or when a question names refit_of (1,000 free fits a month, then $0.01 each); refusals and not_yet bill no decisions, and the samples are free
post.x-dg-cost: one decision per answered case; the first ask on a record, or a question with refit_of, also runs a fit

post.description: For a record asked about more than once, or too large to send inline; a one-off ask can carry its record inline (data.rows, data.csv or data.fetch_url on dg_ask) instead. Stores a record (any shape) so later asks can name it by dataset_id. Free. Takes rows or csv (up to 10,000 rows or 3,000,000 characters, and 4.5 MB, per call), a fetch_url to download (up to 50 MB), or upload: true for large files: it returns upload_page, a link a person opens in a browser to drop in a CSV of up to 250 MB (valid one hour), and upload_url, a presigned URL a program PUTs the file to. Calling again with the returned dataset_id and more rows appends a piece; pieces append in order until the first ask or preflight seals the dataset, and a piece with different columns is refused. Returns dataset_id, status (ready | open | awaiting_upload), rows and columns. A stored dataset is deleted 24 hours after it was last used, or at once with dg_delete_dataset

post.description: For an ask that came back with status pending and a task_id; the later pages of a finished answer come from dg_page instead. Free. Returns the current status of a pending task (a first ask on a large record): status pending (with stage and elapsed_ms) until it finishes, then the same object the original call would have returned, paged the same way over MCP. retry_after_ms is the suggested wait between polls. Re-sending the original call instead would start a second fit. Results are kept for 24 hours

post.description: For checking one table before its first ask; the list of questions a table could be asked comes from dg_suggest instead. Free; fits nothing. Reports whether a table is worth asking about before the first ask: grain (whether one row is one kind of thing), resolutions (what each column's values are; an ambiguous column is not a sound predictor), and fitness (positives per usable predictor over labeled rows). blocking entries mean an answer from this table would not be believable; advisory entries are worth reading. It reports and refuses nothing, and a clean preflight does not promise a pattern exists. Like an ask, it seals a dataset still taking pieces. Tables only

post.description: For outcomes that arrived for cases a model_ref answered; an action taken on a case is recorded with dg_attest instead. Free. Records the real outcome for cases answered under a model_ref: outcome is yes/no (0/1, true/false), observed_at is when it was observed, event_id is the caller's idempotency key. Outcomes are evidence about the model's track record; they do not change a model or an answer. A batch is all or nothing: one bad row writes nothing, and the invalid_outcomes problem lists every bad row by index; with partial: true the valid rows are written and results reports each row. Needs the write:outcomes capability: a person signed in through an MCP host has it; an API key has it when created with "Can report outcomes"

post.description: For deciding whether a refitted model is kept, replaced or abandoned; how a model's calls fared against reported outcomes is dg_track_record instead. Free. For a model_ref from an ask that named refit_of, compares the new fit with the old: pattern is unchanged | changed | no_prior, and recommendation is keep | refit | abandon | no_check_yet (nothing has been compared yet, so it is no reason to renew a model). The chain is built by asking again on the new version of a record with refit_of set to the previous model_ref. A single refusal on a refresh is not drift

post.description: For checking a Verdict before anyone relies on it; the SDKs' verify_offline checks the same signature with no call to Datagoat. Free, and needs no key over REST. Checks that a Verdict is genuine and unaltered. Takes the verdict and signature exactly as received (re-serialising them breaks the signature). Returns status: valid | invalid_signature | expired | unknown_key. An expired Verdict is stale and its question can be asked again. Public keys: https://api.datagoat.io/.well-known/jwks.json

post.description: For recording that a case was acted on through one of its levers; what then happened to the case is dg_report_outcomes instead. Free. Records that a case was acted on through one of its levers, so dg_evidence can compare cases acted on with cases not acted on. Takes the model_ref of the answer, the case's entity_id, the lever_token from that case's levers, the feature's new value after the action (post_value) and when the action happened (acted_at). The engine checks the new value against the lever's target without revealing the target, and returns compliant, dose_fraction (how far toward the target the case moved, 0 to 1) and evaluated_feature (the feature the token checks). Each lever is one feature with its own lever_token; a lever on a category column carries to_one_of, the values that count as acting on it. Only compliant actions count as acted; a non-compliant one leaves the case in neither group. Idempotent by event_id. Needs the write:outcomes capability: a person signed in through an MCP host has it; an API key has it when created with "Can report outcomes"

post.description: For measuring whether acting on the answers changed outcomes; whether the calls themselves were right is dg_track_record instead. Free. For a model_ref, compares the reported outcomes of cases that were acted on (a compliant dg_attest) with cases that were not. live is null until each group has 30 cases with a reported outcome; then it gives n_acted, n_not_acted, rate_acted, rate_not_acted, diff and its confidence interval (ci_low, ci_high), with small_n true below 100 per group. progress always counts cases with an outcome, acted and not acted, so the gap to the floor is visible. The comparison is observational: acted cases were chosen, not randomised

post.summary: How the model's calls held up
post.description: For showing whether a model's calls were right; whether acting on them worked is dg_evidence instead. Free. For a model_ref, sets what the model said about each case against what then happened (the outcomes sent with dg_report_outcomes). Each outcome is paired with the latest answer about that case given on or before the day it was observed; an outcome with no earlier answer is counted in outcomes_without_an_earlier_answer, not paired. overall, and each entry of by_band, by_level and by_chance, give calls, happened, observed_rate, its 95% interval (interval_95) and mean_chance, the average chance the model gave: a calibrated model's observed_rate sits near its mean_chance. A case reported more than once counts once, with its latest outcome. small_n is true below 100 calls. Kept: yesno and score answers, and the top_k cases of a rank (so a rank's by_chance leans high); choice answers are not kept. Answers are kept from records_since on

post.description: For the words, excluded columns, fixed columns (no lever offered) and display of one namespace (one of a builder's customers), set once; the answers themselves come from dg_ask. Free. The profile of a namespace (one of your customers): the words its answers use, columns never used, columns no lever touches, and what its end users see. Sent with words, exclude, fixed or display, it replaces the whole profile (a field left out is reset); sent with only namespace (or nothing, for the workspace itself), it returns the current one. words: case (what a case is called, e.g. customer), outcome (the outcome in plain words, e.g. cancels), columns (a phrase per column, e.g. {"tenure_months": "months as a customer"}). exclude: columns of a table record that no fit in this namespace uses (a new fit, so a new model_ref); the columns that frame a question (outcome, entity, time, group) and columns the record lacks are left out of it, and a shaped record or a model_ref question is not affected (the answer's profile.exclusions_applied says whether they were used). fixed: columns an action never changes (tenure, age, a signup date); the model still reads them, no lever is offered on them, and answers list them in excluded_columns with why fixed_by_caller. display: chance (default) or bands; with bands, the sentence each case carries names its band, and the answer says display bands, a signal for an end-user surface to show bands only (the API still returns every chance). Each answer in the namespace then carries profile {hash, display, exclusions_applied} and, per case, says: one sentence built from these words and the engine's own values, verbatim. Each Verdict names the profile's hash.

post.description: For the rest of an answer that came back paged over MCP (page.next_cursor); an ask still running is dg_poll instead, and the whole answer at once is page.answer_url. Free. Returns the next page of an answer that was too large for one response, from page.next_cursor. Each answer in the page keeps its type, state and model_ref, and its list (cases, or ranked for rank) carries page {offset, returned, total}. Pages are slices of the stored answer in its original order; the last page has no next_cursor. Cursors last as long as the answer: 24 hours

post.summary: Which questions are worth trying on this table?
post.description: For an unfamiliar table: the yes/no questions worth trying on it; asking one is dg_ask, and checking a question already chosen is dg_preflight. Free; fits nothing. Lists the yes/no questions a table could be asked, worth trying first, and says for each whether it is worth asking. Candidates are the table's two-valued columns (converted, churned, lapsed), plus, with include_categories, each value of a column with 3 to 8 values (plan = pro). Each candidate carries outcome_column, positive_values, the share of rows that are yes (prevalence), worth_asking (the engine's quick check that the record holds enough distinct patterns to try; it runs no fit), defined_by (columns that on their own almost completely determine the outcome, so the question restates the data rather than predicts it) and a ready-to-send question. worth_asking is a screen, not an answer: measured on 267 candidate questions across 15 records, it passed 60 of the 65 that dg_ask answered, and about half of the questions it passes are answered. Tables only; entity_column and time_column are never candidates

post.description: For keeping a model answering past its model_expires_at, typically after dg_drift says keep; a model no longer wanted is removed with dg_delete_model instead. Free. Sets a model to expire the given number of days from now (1 to 365), so it keeps answering model_ref questions without a new fit. An expired model cannot be renewed. Returns model_ref and model_expires_at. A model holds cut points and the category values it groups, never rows

post.description: For retiring a model now (dg_drift said abandon, or a customer left); a stored record is removed with dg_delete_dataset instead. Free. Deletes a model now: its model_ref stops answering, and outcome reports, attestations and evidence for it stop too; its Verdicts can still be verified. Asking about the same record again fits (and counts) a new model. Deleting again returns the same result. Without this call a model stops answering when it expires. Needs the write:outcomes capability (a person signed in through an MCP host has it; an API key has it when created with "Can report outcomes")

get.description: The link in export.results_url (CSV, one row per question per case) or page.answer_url (JSON, exactly the REST answer). The signed token is the credential, like a presigned URL: no key is sent, and it lasts 24 hours from when the answer finished. The body is streamed.

404.description: Not a link Datagoat issued, or altered (unknown_link).

410.description: The answer is no longer kept (answer_expired).

post.description: No credential needed. Returns a dgk_test_ key that works on the sample datasets only. Rate-limited per address. For your own data, create a live key at https://datagoat.io/keys.

bearer.description: A dgk_live_ / dgk_test_ key, or an OAuth access token.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem. `code` and `remedy` say what went wrong and what changes the outcome; `field` names the argument at fault; `doc_url` is the code's entry on https://datagoat.io/docs/errors.

errors.description: invalid_outcomes only: every bad field of the batch, one entry each (a row with two bad fields appears twice), in the caller's field names.

retry_after_ms.description: rate_limited only: how long to wait before retrying.

data.description: The record: rows of past cases with a yes/no outcome (or, with shape, data the outcome is read from). Exactly one of dataset_id, rows, csv, fetch_url. Inline data is deleted when the call ends. Optional only when every question names a model_ref and the cases are rows.

dataset_id.description: A dataset from dg_add_dataset (ds_…), or a free sample (sample:…; dg_describe lists them).

rows.description: Inline rows, one object per case. Up to 10,000 rows; dg_add_dataset stores more.

csv.description: Inline CSV text with a header row, up to 3,000,000 characters.

fetch_url.description: A public https URL Datagoat downloads the CSV from. No redirects; private and internal hosts are refused.

fetch_headers.description: Headers to send with fetch_url, e.g. an Authorization header for a private object.

entity_column.description: The column naming each case, e.g. customer_id.

subject_kind.description: What each case is. person turns on decision-support safeguards.

type.description: yesno: the chance the outcome happens. score: that chance as a level. choice: the best option (needs outcome_is_desirable), with each option's chance, most_likely and least_likely. rank: cases in order of the chance.

outcome_column.description: The yes/no column to learn. Required except for choice with option_outcomes.

outcome_is_desirable.description: true when the outcome is one you WANT (converted, renewed, repaid); false when you want to avoid it (churned, defaulted, failed). Optional except on choice; when absent, Datagoat does not fill it in.

positive_values.description: Values of the outcome column that mean yes. Omit when the column has two values such as 0/1, true/false or yes/no.

levels.description: score only. Level names, lowest first. Default: unlikely, possible, likely, very_likely.

cuts.description: score only. One fewer than levels, strictly ascending. Default: 0.25, 0.50, 0.75.

option_column.description: choice only. A column you control (team, channel, offer, contract). Each case is scored once per option, and the best option is named.

options.description: choice with option_column: the values to try.

option_outcomes.description: choice only, other form: {option: outcome_column}, one learned outcome per option (2 to 32).

top_k.description: rank only. How many to return. Default 20.

refit_of.description: The model_ref of an earlier answer on an older version of this record. Adds a drift report, and links the two for dg_drift. A question with refit_of always runs its fit, even on a record asked about before, so the refit is recorded; it counts as a fit.

model_ref.description: Answer from an existing model instead of learning from the record: the model_ref of an earlier answer. Nothing is fitted. The cases are cases.rows, or cases.ids read from the data sent with this call (a newer version of the record, say). The outcome, its yes values and outcome_is_desirable are the model's own. Not for choice. Works until the model's model_expires_at.

cases.description: The cases to answer about. Required for yesno, score and choice. Omit for rank to rank the whole record.

ids.description: Cases already in the record, by entity id. With several rows per id, the latest wins (see time_column).

rows.description: New cases, one object per case. Each needs the entity column and every column the model uses.

time_column.description: The time column. Orders rows, so cases by id take each id's latest row. Required with every shape except table.

shape.description: How to read the record when it is not one row per case: an event log, a series, a panel, signals, traces, or snapshots (an event log plus a snapshot table: each case as it was at each moment). Omit for a table. The engine reads the record into rows per case before it fits; with a model_ref question, an events or snapshots record is read with the columns that model's fit chose. dg_describe lists each shape with a ready-to-run ask.

kind.description: table: one row per case (the default). events: an event log, many rows per case. series: a time series per case, one row per case per period, with an outcome on each row. panel: periods per case, with the outcome read from a column's trend or final window. signals: timestamped sensor readings, with fault or event intervals in the same table. traces: a log of runs (one row per run) with agent, task or tool columns. snapshots: an event log read as of moments you choose, one case per row of a snapshot table (a deal as it entered each stage), with the outcome in the snapshot table.

event_column.description: events, signals, snapshots: the column naming the event type.

value_columns.description: series (required): the numeric columns to summarise over trailing windows. events, snapshots: amounts to sum and average.

event_start_column.description: signals: when an event interval starts. A row with an event_column value is an interval, not a reading.

event_end_column.description: signals: when an event interval ends.

label.description: events (required): {lapsed: true}, or {name, when}. panel (required): {trend_of, direction?, alpha?}, or {window_of, periods?, agg?}.

anyOf.description: 1 when the case has no event at all in the horizon at the end of the log.

name.description: Lowercase, digits and underscores. Becomes the outcome column {name}_next_{horizon}{unit}, e.g. churn_next_24h.

when.description: 1 when ANY event in the horizon at the end of the log matches. A leaf is {column, op, value}; combine leaves with {all: [...]} or {any: [...]}.

trend_of.description: A numeric column. The outcome is 1 when this column shows a significant trend across the case's periods.

window_of.description: A yes/no column observed each period. The outcome is its value over the last periods of each case.

periods.description: How many final periods form the outcome window. Default 1.

agg.description: How the window's values combine. Default max: yes if any period says yes.

horizon_days.description: events, older form (days only): the outcome window at the end of the log. horizon: {value, unit} is the newer form.

lookback_days.description: events, older form (days only): the two activity windows before the outcome window; lookback with horizon is the newer form. snapshots: the two activity windows before each snapshot, in days. Default [30, 90].

lookback.description: events, with horizon {value, unit}: the two activity windows before the outcome window, in the horizon's unit. Default: the unit's first pair (days [30, 90], hours [6, 24], steps [5, 20], ...).

time_unit.description: series: what the time column counts. steps for a whole-number column (a turn, a cycle); otherwise it is read as a time. Default days.

windows.description: series (required): trailing windows in periods, one of [3, 6], [7, 30], [4, 12]. signals (required): in snapshots, one of [1, 3, 7], [3, 7, 30], [1, 7, 30].

snapshot_every.description: signals (required): one snapshot of each case per this period.

horizon.description: events: {value, unit}, the outcome window at the end of the log, in minutes, hours, days, weeks or steps (e.g. {value: 24, unit: 'hours'}). signals (required): a number of SNAPSHOTS (1, 3, 7 or 30); a snapshot's outcome is 1 when an event starts within that many snapshots, so 3 at 6h is 18 hours.

min_history.description: signals: readings a snapshot needs (3, 5 or 10; default 3). panel: periods a case needs (2, 3, 5 or 8).

as_of.description: events, signals: the end of the log, ISO-8601 (or a whole step, with unit steps). Default: the latest time in the data.

snapshots.description: snapshots (required): the snapshot table, one row per case at the moment it is scored (a deal as it entered each stage), with the same entity column as the event log, a snapshot id, the snapshot's time and the outcome. Exactly one of dataset_id, rows, csv, fetch_url.

dataset_id.description: A dataset from dg_add_dataset, or a sample.

snapshot_id_column.description: snapshots (required): the snapshot table's id column; cases.ids name snapshots by it.

snapshot_time_column.description: snapshots (required): when each snapshot was taken. Each snapshot's features count events at or before this moment.

outcome_time_column.description: snapshots: when each snapshot's outcome happened. A snapshot taken at or after its own outcome is left out and counted.

band.description: Advanced. Adds band (act, escalate, refuse), band_reason and max_autonomy to each case.

acknowledge_decision_support.description: Required true when subject_kind is person: results are decision support, with a human in the loop.

export.description: csv adds export.results_url: a CSV of every case (chance, level or choice, reasons), downloadable for 24 hours. The answer itself is unchanged.

model_ttl_days.description: How long a model this call FITS stays usable, in days (1 to 365; default 90). A question answered from an existing fit keeps that model's own expiry. Every answer states model_expires_at; dg_extend_model renews a model.

group_column.description: For a table with several rows per case (the same deal at each stage, all with that deal's outcome): the column naming the case each row belongs to. namespace.description: Keeps this call's models apart from the rest of the workspace, e.g. one namespace per customer of your product. A model fitted in a namespace answers only there, and usage is recorded per namespace. Omit for the workspace's own models.

response_format.description: full (default): every answer with its signed Verdicts. concise: the same answers without verdicts; each answer says verdicts_withheld {count}, and the whole answer, Verdicts included, stays at page.answer_url for 24 hours. idempotency_key.description: A retry with the same key returns the first call's answer without fitting or billing again (keys are kept 24 hours).

status.description: pending: the first fit on a large record is still running; dg_poll with task_id returns the result.

stage.description: pending only: how far the task has got.

elapsed_ms.description: pending only: time since the call was made.

progress.description: pending only, while the engine is fitting: its stage, how far along, and facts about the record so far (rows, the outcome, rows held out); no chance and no finding.

frac.description: How far along, 0 to 1, across the call's fits.

page.description: Only when the answer is larger than one MCP response: this response is its first page.

next_cursor.description: Absent on the last page. dg_page with this cursor returns the next page.

export.description: With export: csv, a download of every case as CSV. Valid 24 hours; the link is the credential.

state.description: The answer's status, the first field that matters. answered: the record supports an answer. refused: the record holds no pattern that holds on held-out rows (reasons no_finding_cleared), or it has too few usable predictor columns to search (reasons too_few_predictors, with needs.columns and have.columns); the same call returns the same refusal. not_yet: too few labeled rows or positives (rows where the outcome happened) to check a model; reasons name what is short (too_few_labeled_rows, too_few_positives, no_positives when the outcome's yes values match no row, too_few_to_hold_out when neither count explains it), needs says how many more of each (0 when that one is not short), and have says what the record holds.

next.description: The operations that make sense after this answer, each with its cost and what it gives. Data, not instructions.

fixed.description: Columns an action never changes (tenure, age, a signup date): the model still reads them, no lever is offered on them, and answers list them in excluded_columns with why fixed_by_caller.

cursor.description: page.next_cursor from the previous response, exactly as given.

state.description: The answer's status, the first field that matters. answered: the record supports an answer. refused: the record holds no pattern that holds on held-out rows (reasons no_finding_cleared), or it has too few usable predictor columns to search (reasons too_few_predictors, with needs.columns and have.columns); the same call returns the same refusal. not_yet: too few labeled rows or positives (rows where the outcome happened) to check a model; reasons name what is short (too_few_labeled_rows, too_few_positives, no_positives when the outcome's yes values match no row, too_few_to_hold_out when neither count explains it), needs says how many more of each (0 when that one is not short), and have says what the record holds.

decision.description: The state as a decision: actionable when answered, else not_yet or refused. A pure mapping of state, no new number. Per case, band (with band: true) and not_scoreable still apply.

next.description: The operations that make sense after this answer, each with its cost and what it gives. Data, not instructions.

with.description: The input that makes it this step, e.g. model_ref or refit_of.

cache.description: Known values: hit, miss; others may be added.

model_expires_at.description: When this answer's model stops answering, ISO-8601 UTC. For choice, the earliest of its models. dg_extend_model renews it.

quality.description: How the model was measured: realised_lift, top_decile_lift, validation_scheme, confidence_tier, and held_out {whole_cases_by} when every row of one case was held out together (the accuracy is on cases the model never saw).

model_columns.description: yesno, score and rank: every column a case must carry for this model, in your column names. A scheduled job scoring by model_ref sends these.

pattern.description: The pattern the model found: the conditions under which the outcome is most common in the record, with their cut points. Describes the group, not a rule; each case's pattern_match says how many it meets. Not on choice.

one_of_more.description: How many more values the group holds than one_of lists (lists stop at 25).

text.description: The same bounds in words, e.g. "tenure_months 9 to under 17" (numbers to 6 significant digits).

missing.description: The condition is a blank value alone (text says "… is missing").

missing_matches.description: true: a blank value counts as meeting this condition, and text says so (e.g. "region is west or is missing").

unseen_values.description: Per column, the values the model cannot read: a category it never saw, text outside the levels it learned, or a non-number where it reads a number.
